text:
maya: Quick heads-up — after enabling late-hop speculative on llamaX-13b-4bit in staging I'm seeing a 4–7% drop on EVAL-SMALLQA (EM). Anyone else hit this?

reza: Hmm. Did you run with same sampling settings? Sometimes speculative hops + quantization change deterministic ordering.

maya: config I used:
```
model: llamaX-13b-4bit
decode: late_hop=true
hop_prob: 0.25
early_exit: false
kv_warm: true
batch_size: 1
seed: 42
```
Quick metric snippet (EM over 1000 examples):
```
baseline (fp16, no-late-hop): 72.8
late_hop (4bit, hop=0.25): 68.9
```
Also seeing hallucination cases in longer answers.

al: Could be alignment drift from skipping the KV refill path. Lower hop_prob or force a KV-sync every N tokens helps. Try hop_prob=0.15 and kv_warm=false as a sanity check.

deploy-bot: deploy to staging completed for commit c3f7a2 (maya/late-hop-experiment) :white_check_mark:

reza: Also check top_k/top_p and temperature — quant can amplify small distribution shifts. If you used greedy vs temp0.0 it could change WM.

toni: I can run a 3-way ablation (hop=0, hop=0.15, hop=0.25) with same seeds and batch configs. Give me 30m.

maya: Thanks — will hold off any prod flips. Also note dropout: None. I can attach a few example prompts that regress.

sam: Also run the FP16 baseline with the exact same decode pipeline (late-hop disabled) but with the quant runtime's tokenization hooks — isolates quant vs decode change.

reza: queued a CI job:
`/ci run --job=spec-latehop-13b-quant-abl --variants=hop0.0,hop0.15,hop0.25 --seeds=42,84 --batch=1`

ci-bot: Job queued (#1234). ETA ~12m. We will post results to this thread.

toni: :thumbsup: I'll paste the ablation table when ready.

maya: appreciated — saving the sample set now and will attach when CI posts.

sam: If regressions persist on hop=0.0, it's likely quantization artifact; if only with hop>0 then decode interaction. Either way we should add a small regression test to onboarding harness.

maya: Agreed. I'll add a quick EM/regression check to the model-onboard job. Thanks all.
